{"version":"2b1","blocks":[{"type":"text","text":"The dot product of two vectors is a scalar value that represents how much one vector extends in the direction of another. Geometrically, it is the product of the length of the first vector and the length of the projection of the second vector onto the first."},{"type":"ui","source":"protocol v2b1

$angle = integer 0 180

root = Stack([definition, diagram, interactive])

definition = Text("The dot product of two vectors A and B is defined as |A| * |B| * cos(θ), where θ is the angle between them. It measures how much B points in the direction of A.")

diagram = Graphic("Dot Product Diagram", group([vectorA, vectorB, projectionB, angleArc, labels]))

vectorA = path("M 50 100 L 200 100", "black", 2)
vectorB = path("M 50 100 L " + (50 + 150 * cos($angle * 3.14159 / 180)) + " " + (100 - 150 * sin($angle * 3.14159 / 180)), "blue", 2)
projectionB = path("M 50 100 L " + (50 + 150 * cos($angle * 3.14159 / 180)) + " 100", "red", 2)
angleArc = path("M 180 100 A 20 20 0 0 1 " + (180 + 20 * cos($angle * 3.14159 / 180)) + " " + (100 - 20 * sin($angle * 3.14159 / 180)), "green", 1)
labels = group([
  text(120, 90, "A", "black"),
  text(150, 50, "B", "blue"),
  text(120, 110, "Projection of B on A", "red")
])

interactive = Control("Angle between vectors (degrees)", 0, 180, [], $angle)","state":[{"name":"angle","value":60}]},{"type":"text","text":"When the angle θ is 90 degrees, the vectors are orthogonal, and their dot product is zero because the projection length is zero. This means they have no component in each other's direction.

If the angle is greater than 90 degrees, the cosine is negative, so the dot product is negative. This corresponds to a negative projection, meaning the vectors point in more opposite than same directions."}]}

Names start with ASCII letter, then alphanumeric or underscore, at most 48 characters. All declarations must be reachable. Text and labels at most 512 characters. Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
One assignment per physical line. root = Stack([leafName, otherLeaf]). Each leaf is one named call: Text("text"), Metric("label",numericValue), Control("label",literalMin,literalMax,choices,$variable), Table([{label:"name",score:number}]), Graphic("label",items). Declare $variable = integer and bind it to exactly one Control. Use [] for range or literal string options indexed 0..n-1. Derived name = expression. Strings use double quotes. Numeric + - * /, == > <, condition ? yes : no, arrays, objects, named references, @Sum(numbers), @Sort(rows,"score","desc") are allowed. No unary minus, concatenation, member access, map, interpolation or inline nested components. Produce complete root and definitions.
Choose text for a simple definition. Use a legible diagram if spatial relationships aid understanding. Use controls for a changing decision. Label units, state assumptions, use short readable labels, give each output an informative name and check zero or boundary conditions. Keep geometry inside the viewBox.
